research_mode: official HSE and GOV.UK primary guidance only; gas, asbestos, smoke/carbon-monoxide alarm and residential fire-safety regulatory and methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Small-block fire guide scope
verified_claims: The small-block guide covers qualifying purpose-built or later-compliant converted blocks limited to three storeys and no more than six flats.
limitations: Buildings outside the stated design and size scope require other guidance.

sources.name: Fire-law building-element scope
verified_claims: The guide applies to common parts as well as the building structure, external walls and doors between flats and common parts.
limitations: Scope under fire law is not evidence that those elements are compliant.

sources.name: Responsible-person examples for small blocks
verified_claims: Potential responsible persons include social housing providers, private landlords, freeholders, resident management companies, right-to-manage companies and managing agents.
limitations: The actual responsible person must be established from control and legal arrangements.

sources.name: Fire risk-assessment duty
verified_claims: Responsible persons should complete and maintain a suitable fire risk assessment for the premises within scope.
limitations: The existence or quality of an assessment cannot be inferred from the building category.

sources.name: Stay-put design assumption
verified_claims: The guide is based on qualifying blocks designed around a stay-put strategy.
limitations: A stay-put strategy must not be assumed where design or compartmentation differs materially.

sources.name: Fire-origin flat evacuation principle
verified_claims: Under the described stay-put approach, occupants of the flat where fire occurs should evacuate.
limitations: Real incidents may require different action based on conditions and fire-service instructions.

sources.name: Other-flat stay-put principle
verified_claims: Occupants of other flats are normally safe to remain unless their flat is affected by fire or smoke or the fire and rescue service instructs them to leave.
limitations: The guidance does not guarantee safety in every incident or building.

sources.name: Stay-put voluntary-exit boundary
verified_claims: A stay-put strategy does not prevent occupants from leaving if they choose and can do so safely.
limitations: Leaving through smoke-affected common parts may increase risk.

sources.name: Compartmentation support for stay-put
verified_claims: Adequate fire-resisting compartmentation is essential to support the stay-put strategy.
limitations: Original design intent does not prove that compartmentation remains intact.

sources.name: Common-parts fire design assumption
verified_claims: The guide assumes a low probability of fire in common parts and that any such fire is limited in extent.
limitations: The assumption is a design basis, not an observed condition for a particular block.

sources.name: Fire-safety contractor competence
verified_claims: Responsible persons should ensure contractors are competent, while ultimate responsibility for compliance remains with the responsible person.
limitations: Certification can support competence checks but does not guarantee compliant work.

sources.name: Fire Safety Act clarified scope
verified_claims: The Fire Safety Act clarified that fire-risk assessments cover building structure, external walls and individual flat entrance doors between dwellings and common parts.
limitations: Legal coverage does not establish the physical condition of those elements.

sources.name: Multiple responsible persons
verified_claims: More than one Responsible Person may exist within the same building where different parties control workplaces or fire-safety matters.
limitations: The allocation of duties requires building-specific legal and operational evidence.

sources.name: Medium and high-rise additional fire duties
verified_claims: The Fire Safety (England) Regulations introduced additional duties for medium-rise and high-rise blocks, including information and safety-measure requirements.
limitations: Height classification and applicable duties must be verified from reliable building data.

sources.name: Fire guidance non-exhaustive boundary
verified_claims: The Home Office describes its responsibilities guidance as a high-level, non-exhaustive summary.
limitations: Premises-specific risk assessment and legal advice may be needed; the summary must not be used as a complete compliance determination.
